ads.label: INTERNAL SPONSOR
ads.title: Mark Agency Coffee Substitute
lines: It may not be coffee, but it does technically increase alertness.
Approved for overnight stakeouts, paperwork emergencies and regrettable Monday meetings.
Mark Agency Coffee Substitute: now with 14 percent less existential dread.

ads.label: ADVERTISEMENT
ads.title: Professor Bell’s Rope Polish
lines: Second-story entry should still feel refined.
Professor Bell’s Rope Polish: grip, elegance, and a respectable scent of cedar.
Now available in travel size and suspiciously enormous trunk size.

ads.label: ADVERTISEMENT
ads.title: Marlowe Lock & Key Academy
lines: Need to understand locks for entirely respectable reasons?
Enroll now and receive a complimentary brass practice tumbler.
Marlowe Lock & Key Academy: education with discretion.

ads.label: ADVERTISEMENT
ads.title: Mr. Key – 24-Hour Locksmith
lines: Lock jammed? Safe feeling temperamental?
Mr. Key: we open everything. Officially — legal property only.
Call before you start experimenting with a lockpick.

ads.label: ADVERTISEMENT
ads.title: Raj Rapid Courier
lines: Parcels that must arrive before anyone notices they were gone.
Raj Rapid Courier: bazaar-to-museum express routes available.
Special packaging for "fragile" and "rare" items.

ads.label: ADVERTISEMENT
ads.title: Liberty Lockbox Inc.
lines: Some secrets deserve more than a drawer.
Liberty Lockbox: private vaults, 24/7 access, staff trained to forget faces.
Ask for our "anonymous patron" tier at the desk.

fillers.label: INTERNAL TRAINING
fillers.title: Performance Review: You Are the Problem
lines: Remember: a tidy desk is a tidy mind. A tidy alibi is a tidy career.
This week's employee of the month is unavailable for comment and possibly in Lisbon.
Next: how to request a new trench coat without calling it operational equipment.

fillers.label: LIFESTYLE
fillers.title: Antique Appetite
lines: Can ceremonial bowls improve soup? We remain unconvinced.
However, plating with dynastic arrogance continues to test very well.
After the break: ten herbs most likely to alarm a museum guard.

fillers.label: GAME SHOW
fillers.title: Crossword Extra
lines: Today's main clue has seven letters and fits the word "theft" rather suspiciously well.
Viewers are kindly asked not to call the museum while the programme is live.
After the break: can a curator be both a witness and an avid crossword enthusiast?

fillers.label: REPORTAGE
fillers.title: Ordnung im Archiv
lines: Tonight we explore the mysterious world of archival access codes.
Some seals open doors. Some locks open files. Some officials open nothing.
Our guest insists "no one" could reproduce the royal seal from memory. We raise an eyebrow.

fillers.label: LIFESTYLE
fillers.title: Biscuits & Betrayal
lines: The Great Biscuit Championship takes an unexpected turn when someone's shortbread disappears.
One judge insists it was simply "relocated for safety".
Another mutters something about "Tower security" and refuses to elaborate.

fillers.label: CULINARY
fillers.title: Masala Aur Mysteries
lines: Tonight: recipes that double as ciphers.
Each ingredient stands for a star, each star stands for a vault.
Viewers are reminded not to apply this recipe directly to museum security guards.

fillers.label: DOCU-SERIES
fillers.title: The Apartment Hunt
lines: A man searches Manhattan for a two-bedroom under four thousand dollars.
The search reveals secret storage spaces, unmarked doors, and one suspiciously large lockbox.
Tonight's episode is filed under "real estate". It probably shouldn't be.
